distractors: To restate something at greater length, on the assumption that more words will do what fewer of them did not.
To condense a long argument down to its essentials, so that somebody can carry the whole of it out of the room in one sentence.

To make something deliberately hard to follow, so that the plain version of it never quite surfaces. The direction of travel is away from understanding rather than towards it, and the effort is the giveaway.

To supply the evidence that backs up a claim, so that somebody else can check the working rather than simply take your word for it. What was missing was the proof, and the claim itself was perfectly clear all along.

To infer a conclusion from information that is plainly incomplete, filling the gaps with judgement and marking which parts were filled that way. You are producing something that was never on the page, which is a different job from making sense of what is.
